data.description:
## Context

Agents routinely refer to tickets by the first four hexadecimal characters of the canonical UUID instead of the ticket's human-readable alias. Four-character prefixes are increasingly collision-prone as the store grows, while aliases are designed to be user-friendly and substantially less likely to collide.

## Observed reproduction

During a read-only reassessment of 94 tickets, the agent initially passed four-character prefixes to `rebar summary`. The command rejected multiple inputs as ambiguous:

- `2dce` matched `2dce-1c25-ff43-48c6` and `2dce-d7b9-6574-4f62`
- `2e89` matched `2e89-061c-1784-48c4` and `2e89-2e6f-041f-4d77`
- `615c` matched `615c-7646-4566-4bb8` and `615c-df86-c653-424b`
- `b2bb` matched `b2bb-2ac7-5ce3-4412` and `b2bb-fa81-e054-4fb5`
- `8fbd` matched `8fbd-5e8c-ce58-495b` and `8fbd-e9d5-326e-40d8`

The aliases were available in ticket state, but the agent selected prefixes without first resolving them. This is an agent-facing usability and affordance failure, not merely a resolver correctness problem: the resolver correctly refused ambiguous identifiers.

## Investigation plan

- Inventory agent instructions, CLI help, examples, summaries, list/search projections, MCP schemas, and ticket-rendering surfaces to determine which identifier form they foreground.
- Trace why agents copy four-character UUID prefixes: missing aliases in common output, examples that normalize short prefixes, token-saving pressure, or resolver ergonomics.
- Compare alias availability and uniqueness guarantees with canonical IDs and dynamically unique prefixes.
- Identify the smallest durable intervention: foreground aliases, emit collision-safe references, strengthen agent guidance, or make convenience output choose the shortest currently unique prefix instead of a fixed four characters.
- Validate the intervention against representative multi-ticket agent workflows.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The preference for four-character prefixes over aliases is reproduced in at least one representative agent workflow and grounded in the exact prompt/output/interface affordance that caused it.
- [ ] Root cause distinguishes agent-instruction behavior from missing/poorly ranked alias data and from resolver behavior.
- [ ] Current alias presence, uniqueness semantics, and collision behavior are documented from code and tests.
- [ ] A proposed repair makes the preferred agent-visible reference collision-safe without weakening the resolver's fail-closed ambiguous-prefix behavior.
- [ ] Regression coverage proves representative multi-ticket workflows no longer emit or depend on ambiguous fixed four-character prefixes.
- [ ] CLI, MCP, library, and documentation parity are assessed before implementation.
data.title: Agents choose collision-prone 4-character ticket prefixes instead of user-friendly aliases
